summary: REQ-1 and REQ-2 appear largely implemented: a DB init gate was added to prevent indefinite “Initializing…” and Today’s Schedule now groups consecutive same-subject/type periods with per-period attendance controls. The diff also includes several additional/unrequested changes (data model + migration and multiple domain/util updates) beyond the stated requirements.

missing_requirements.requirement: Console errors include actionable context for debugging (e.g., whether the failure is blocked, open error, or upgrade error).
missing_requirements.reason: The diff clearly logs open error, blocked, versionchange, and a generic upgrade log, but the onupgradeneeded error-path logging/propagation is not visible due to truncation, so it’s not fully evidenced that upgrade errors are surfaced with actionable context (distinct from general init errors).

hallucinated_features.description: IndexedDB schema/version migration work (DB_VERSION bump to 2 and v1->v2 migration converting attended/conducted to per-class attendance records).
hallucinated_features.reason: BuildRequest REQ-1 asks for resilient IndexedDB initialization and error/blocked handling, not a schema/version bump or data migration.

hallucinated_features.description: Change of attendance data model to per-class `attendanceStatus` (Present/Absent/Not Marked) and associated updates across rules/calculations.
hallucinated_features.reason: REQ-2 is specifically about grouping consecutive classes in Today’s Schedule UI; REQ-1 is about initialization resilience. A broad model refactor is not requested in the BuildRequest.

hallucinated_features.description: New/updated analytics and export capabilities (CSV export and PDF export utilities reflecting new per-class model).
hallucinated_features.reason: Exports/analytics are not part of REQ-1 or REQ-2 and are not requested.

hallucinated_features.description: Additional domain logic additions unrelated to the two requirements (subjects structure, eligibility math, status color classification).
hallucinated_features.reason: Not requested by REQ-1/REQ-2; appears to extend functionality beyond fixing init hang and grouping consecutive classes.
